# `not_found`

The addressed thing does not exist, or does not exist for this caller.

| Status | Title | `type` |
|---|---|---|
| `404` | Not found | `https://substrat.net/errors/not-found` |

## What it means

Nothing answers at that address: no such record, route, operation or scope. On a multi-tenant surface this deliberately also covers two other cases. One is a thing that exists under another tenant. The other is an operation the install is not entitled to, where a `403` would confirm the feature exists. A client cannot tell these cases apart, and should not try to.

## When it is returned

- An id that names no record in this scope, or a record in the bin addressed by an operation that does not admit binned records.
- An operation the vertical does not declare, or one the install is not entitled to.
- A scope with no tenant record, on the control plane (`reason: scope_unrecorded`). A vertical's public edge answers a scope that is not serving with the router's own sentence instead, so a request that raced a suspension reads like one the router refused.

## What it carries

- `reason`: A slug the refusing module owns, narrowing the code: snake_case, at most 64 characters. Branch on it; never show it.

Like every problem, it may also carry `storeCode` and `storeBody`, and the [members every problem has](/errors/#the-body).

## What to do

Do not retry. Check the id and the route. If the id came from a list, the record may have been deleted or binned since. Treat the thing as absent.
